waves.name: Bootstrap verification
waves.purpose: Verify durable bootstrap records and repository state without re-evaluating the approved architecture.

waves.name: Foundation
waves.purpose: Establish package, contracts, event durability, and workflow interfaces used by every later worker.

waves.name: Independent boundaries
waves.purpose: Implement isolated adapters and fakes against stable foundation interfaces.

waves.name: Coordination workflows
waves.purpose: Connect agent roles, notifications, GitHub issues, and long-running coding.

waves.name: QA and recovery
waves.purpose: Add independent validation, supervision, reconciliation, and crash recovery.

waves.name: Integrated proof
waves.purpose: Prove the complete workflow and product acceptance criteria.

tasks.title: Create the package, CLI, configuration, and test foundation
acceptance_criteria: The project installs as a Python package using the src layout defined in ARCH.md.
The milburn command exposes a help screen and version output.
Configuration loading has a deterministic public interface and no network side effects.
pytest runs from the repository root with deterministic defaults.
The initial test suite does not launch Codex, tmux, GitHub, or a network connection.

tasks.title: Implement domain contracts, commands, events, states, and errors
acceptance_criteria: Core commands, events, role identifiers, task states, attempt states, and decision contracts match ARCH.md.
Every durable event and external envelope carries a schema version.
Contracts serialize and deserialize without hidden mutable values.
Invalid roles, transitions, identifiers, and malformed envelopes fail with explicit domain errors.

tasks.title: Implement the SQLite event store, projections, and deterministic replay
acceptance_criteria: Events append atomically with an expected stream sequence.
Concurrent stale appends fail rather than silently overwriting or duplicating state.
Pure projections rebuild task, attempt, decision, notification, and external-effect state.
Restarting with the same database reproduces the same projections.
Migrations are versioned and repeatable.

tasks.title: Implement the workflow controller shell and transition guard
acceptance_criteria: The deterministic guard accepts every legal transition and rejects illegal role and lifecycle transitions.
Recommendations from model roles never bypass controller authority.
Command handling records intent before requesting an external effect.
Scheduling respects dependencies and prevents two active Coder attempts for one issue.
Policy tests cover happy paths, illegal transitions, duplicates, and stale commands.

tasks.title: Add concise defect feedback briefs to the bootstrap workflow
acceptance_criteria: Add bootstrap/feedback/README.md defining the feedback purpose, entry format, identifier convention, and retention policy.
Keep one compact Markdown feedback file per task at bootstrap/feedback/<task-id>.md.

Every blocking or meaningful review, test, integration, recovery, or production defect records: feedback ID, discovery phase, severity, symptom, root cause, resolution, fix commit, regression evidence, lesson, and status.
Minor formatting-only corrections may be omitted.
Findings remain linked to the originating task, attempt, worker candidate, coordinator integration, and GitHub PR when available.
A task cannot be marked done until every resolved meaningful finding has fix and regression evidence, while unresolved or separately scoped findings become linked GitHub issues.
PR descriptions include a feedback-summary section and link to the task feedback brief.
Workers may propose entries in their task progress record, but only the coordinator writes or finalizes bootstrap/feedback files.
Feedback briefs do not copy private transcripts, model reasoning, secrets, or large command logs.
Update AGENTS.md, bootstrap/README.md, bootstrap/progress/tasks/TEMPLATE.md, and scripts/smoke-test.sh to enforce the workflow.
Backfill concise briefs for MB-001 through MB-004 using already recorded findings; do not invent missing root causes or evidence.
The smoke test validates naming, required headings, known task IDs, unique feedback IDs, and that resolved entries contain fix and regression evidence.
required_tests: Any focused bootstrap feedback-validation tests added by the task

tasks.title: Implement the tmux runtime and fake runtime
acceptance_criteria: The runtime creates named tmux windows and records durable endpoint identity.
Lifecycle operations verify observable postconditions instead of treating sent keystrokes as success.
Generation and process identity prevent stale endpoint reuse.
A fake runtime supports deterministic ordinary tests without tmux.
Opt-in contract tests exercise a real local tmux installation.

tasks.title: Implement the Codex adapter, launch briefs, and result parsing
acceptance_criteria: The adapter renders bounded role briefs and launches through an injected process/runtime interface.
Result parsing accepts only known schema versions and correlates role, task, and attempt IDs.
Process exit is recorded separately from task success.
A fake Codex adapter supports deterministic scripted results and failures.
Live Codex behavior is isolated behind opt-in contract tests.

tasks.title: Persist per-agent token usage and replayable usage summaries
acceptance_criteria: Milburn records usage against task ID, role, attempt ID, Codex session or endpoint, and model when those values are available.
Usage distinguishes input, output, cached-input, and reasoning tokens when Codex reports them.
Records distinguish partial observations from final totals and prevent cumulative counters from being counted twice.
Missing or unsupported usage is represented explicitly as unavailable; Milburn never invents token counts.
Usage is collected through the Codex adapter semantic boundary, not by scraping terminal colors or human-oriented prose.
Append-only usage events can be replayed into per-attempt, per-task, per-role, and workflow totals.
Restart and duplicate-delivery tests prove usage totals remain deterministic and idempotent.
This is observability only. It does not add prices, budgets, spending limits, reservations, or routing policy.
Later operator views can consume the usage projection without reading private agent transcripts.

tasks.title: Record session compaction and build durable handoff manifests
acceptance_criteria: Milburn represents a logical agent attempt separately from its replaceable Codex session generations.
Adapter observations record compaction, context-usage, and session identity only when supported by a semantic Codex interface; unsupported data is explicitly unavailable.
Versioned events retain task ID, role, attempt ID, session generation, endpoint/session ID, source version, observation time, and whether an observation is partial or final.

A versioned handoff manifest contains role, task and attempt IDs, issue and acceptance criteria references, worktree, branch, base and head SHAs, progress reference, completed and remaining work, exact test evidence, open decisions, inbox/outbox sequence, uncertain external effects, and brief/rules digests.
The handoff manifest contains no private transcript and no fabricated summary of unavailable state.
A replacement session is rejected when the manifest is stale, mismatched to the task or Git state, missing required acknowledgements, or hides an uncertain external effect.
Replay reconstructs session generations and the latest valid handoff checkpoint deterministically.
Duplicate lifecycle observations and restart recovery do not duplicate usage or session transitions.

tasks.title: Add a durable plan-amendment gate before worker dispatch
acceptance_criteria: A user instruction that changes scope, policy, specifications, tasks, dependencies, waves, acceptance criteria, or dispatch rules becomes a pending plan amendment.
New worker dispatch freezes while any plan amendment is pending or coordinator-owned planning files have uncommitted changes.
Existing active work is explicitly classified as unaffected, needs steering, must pause, or must stop.
Unaffected workers may continue; the coordinator must not cancel or restart them merely because an amendment exists.

Every amendment records source/authority, requested change, affected tasks, active-work classification, specification changes, registry changes, GitHub changes, effective commit, and resolution status.
PRD.md, ARCH.md, bootstrap/tasks.json, bootstrap/README.md, and GitHub issue dependencies are reconciled as one reviewed amendment before dispatch resumes.
The coordinator verifies the committed amendment and remote PR merge before declaring it effective.
AGENTS.md, bootstrap/ROOT_PROMPT.md, bootstrap/README.md, and smoke validation enforce the amendment gate.
Startup and final-response preflights detect unresolved amendments.
Define versioned commands/events for amendment request, impact assessment, approval or rejection, application, and dispatch resumption.
Controller policy prevents new AgentLaunchRequested effects while an amendment is pending.
Active attempts retain their generation and ownership until an explicit impact decision changes them.
Applying an amendment uses expected-version concurrency and is replayable and idempotent.
Restart reconciliation preserves pending amendments and never silently applies or drops them.
Operator views explain the amendment, authority, affected work, decision, effective revision, and whether dispatch is frozen.
Tests reproduce the original failure mode: an amendment arrives while workers are active, unaffected workers continue, and no additional worker launches before the amendment is committed and applied.

tasks.title: Implement the skill catalog, role rules, skill packages, and digest validation
acceptance_criteria: All six required role skills exist with valid metadata and only necessary resources.
Role rules remain distinct from procedural skills and encode mandatory authority limits.
The catalog validates referenced resources and records root and resource digests.
Missing, malformed, or changed required skills block launch with an explicit result.
Structural and fixture-based skill tests run without live model calls.

tasks.title: Implement the GitHub gateway, MCP effect journal, and local fakes
acceptance_criteria: A narrow GitHubGateway interface hides MCP tool names and wire formats.
Every mutation has an effect ID and is recorded before invocation.
Timeouts become uncertain effects and are reconciled by reading remote state before retry.
Allow-listed operations prevent agents from obtaining unrestricted mutation authority.
Local fakes cover success, failure, timeout, duplicate, and read-after-write behavior.

tasks.title: Implement the Git worktree manager and fake workspace manager
acceptance_criteria: Every mutating attempt receives one recorded branch, base SHA, and worktree.
Paths are validated before creation, reuse, or retirement.
An environment is never reused until prior ownership and process state are reconciled.
Temporary Git repositories test create, resume, conflict, dirty state, and safe retirement.
Ordinary tests do not modify the user's real repository.

tasks.title: Implement the persistent Coordinator session, notifications, and user decisions
acceptance_criteria: One durable Coordinator endpoint receives actionable notifications while ordinary turns end normally.
Unread notifications survive restart and are drained before unrelated new work.
Worker questions, presented decisions, user answers, and worker acknowledgements retain correlation IDs.
The Coordinator cannot launch processes, mutate GitHub, or approve completion directly.
Scripted integration tests cover unavailable Coordinator and ambiguous user responses.

tasks.title: Implement Planner, Classifier/Router, and Architect coordination
acceptance_criteria: Planner results contain stages, dependencies, risks, and correlated decision requests.
Router proposals contain only known roles and never carry arbitrary commands or credentials.
Architect results contain PRD, ARCH, and dependency-aware issue drafts matching known schemas.
Controller policy validates every proposal before state changes.
Malformed, unknown-version, and unauthorized role results fail deterministically.

tasks.title: Implement the GitHub issue registry and idempotent issue creation
acceptance_criteria: Issue drafts require objective, scope, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and stable Milburn identity.
Controller-owned creation maps issue state to the approved Milburn labels.
Interrupted or timed-out creation is reconciled without duplicate issues.
Agents submit narrow commands and never receive unrestricted GitHub mutation tools.
Scripted integration tests use a local fake MCP server and no network.

tasks.title: Implement the long-running Coder workflow and protocol guard
acceptance_criteria: Each Coder receives exactly one ready issue, one branch, one worktree, and one attempt identity.
Startup requires issue, progress, Git status, issue-specific history, current diff, and smoke-test reconciliation.
Progress records and issue-marked commits are validated before accepting a candidate.
A replacement Coder resumes from durable evidence without the previous transcript.
The Coder cannot close, approve, or mark its own issue done.

The Coder skill and every Coder launch brief carry the six generic boundary questions (PRD 13.1); validators and adapters get negative tests before the happy path, and any fake adapter ships with fake/live parity tests.

Coder test commands run through the shared workspace test environment and bounded command runner (PRD 12.6): one idempotent, concurrency-safe environment per repository outside the worktrees, with the worktree's source on the path, returning a bounded summary with a durable log reference instead of raw output.

tasks.title: Implement independent Tester execution and QA policy
acceptance_criteria: Tester receives the exact candidate SHA, issue acceptance criteria, specifications, and clearly labeled Coder claims.
Validation runs in a clean checkout where practical and records commands and evidence.
QA distinguishes product failure, infrastructure failure, and decisions needed.
Failed QA returns the same issue to coding with evidence.
Only controller policy marks work done after passing independent evidence.

QA rework is bounded by the convergence policy (PRD 12.5): a pure function over recorded rounds (finding identity, category, location, severity, round) that escalates to a user decision when a finding recurs, a round has no fewer blocking findings than the last round that had findings, a fix introduces a new blocking finding in code it touched, or the maximum fix rounds is reached; escalation pauses only that task.

The milburn-qa skill requires enumerating every occurrence of a defect class on the first pass and uses the same boundary questions; fixes are re-tested by blast radius before one full confirmation pass.
Tester commands return bounded summaries (command, result, duration, durable log reference) with the failing excerpt on failure, and run in the shared workspace test environment.

tasks.title: Persist defect resolutions and regression feedback in Milburn
acceptance_criteria: Define versioned contracts and events for DefectObserved, DefectResolutionProposed, DefectResolved, and RegressionEvidenceRecorded, or equivalent approved names.
Every defect links repository, issue/task, role, attempt, session generation when available, candidate SHA, discovery phase, severity, symptom, evidence, and status.
Resolution records link the fix commit, concise root cause, resolution summary, regression command/test, result evidence, and resolver authority.
Replay produces deterministic open-defect, resolved-defect, per-task feedback, and recurring-lesson projections.
Duplicate QA reports, retries, and restart reconciliation do not duplicate defects or regression evidence.
A task cannot reach done while a blocking defect is unresolved or a resolved blocking defect lacks regression evidence.
Failed QA for the same task returns evidence to the Coder; separately scoped defects create linked GitHub issues through controller policy.
Operator APIs/views can show concise defect briefs and links without exposing private transcripts, prompts, secrets, or raw reasoning.
Feedback is evidence, not model memory: a replacement agent reads the concise projection and repository state rather than a previous transcript.
Fixtures and tests cover discovery, correction, re-review, duplicate delivery, restart replay, unresolved blocking defects, and separately scoped follow-up issues.
A defect that matches an earlier resolved defect by category and location is recorded as recurring and counts toward rework escalation (PRD 12.5).

A user-accepted known limitation is a first-class decision: it records the user's authority, keeps the defect open as deferred (never fixed), links a follow-up issue, and can only be created from a recorded user decision, never by a Coder, Tester, Router, or Coordinator.
Recurring lessons are included, bounded and as short references, in the launch briefs of later attempts touching the same area.

tasks.title: Implement role-specific session rotation and replacement policy
acceptance_criteria: A logical role and attempt may span multiple fenced Codex session generations without changing task ownership.
Coordinator policy permits fresh model turns and replacement sessions while durable decisions and notifications remain authoritative.
Coder policy normally keeps one session for one task attempt, does not replace solely because one compaction occurred, and replaces only from a validated checkpoint.
Planner and Architect sessions end at approved artifact boundaries; Classifier/Router calls are short and fresh; Tester always starts fresh from the exact candidate SHA and acceptance criteria.

Replacement triggers include repeated compaction when observable, degraded or contradictory context evidenced against durable state, unrecoverable session failure, explicit independence requirements, or a completed semantic boundary.
Before replacement, Milburn validates Git state, progress, tests, decisions, message acknowledgements, uncertain effects, and handoff freshness.
Session generation fencing prevents late messages or lifecycle commands from reaching a replacement generation.
Recovery never treats unknown as dead and never duplicates external effects.
Usage telemetry compares continuation and replacement costs without making cache assumptions or using token cost as the sole safety decision.
Operator evidence explains why a session continued, rotated, or was replaced.
Final-response and stopping rules remain independent of session replacement; replacing a session is not task completion.

Replacement may also be triggered when observed context use reaches a configured percentage of the model's reported window or an absolute token ceiling, whichever comes first, only at a quiescent point and from a validated checkpoint; unsupported or missing observations never trigger it (PRD 12.4).

Every launch and replacement is generated from durable state as a bounded brief that embeds a source digest, is rejected when stale, and fails closed above a configured size budget; no launch path copies a prior transcript; the first observed input size of each launch is recorded when Codex reports it.
After restart the Coordinator resumes from a bounded state digest of open decisions, unread notifications, active attempts, ready tasks, and blockers.

tasks.title: Implement supervision, reconciliation, crash recovery, and fault handling
acceptance_criteria: Supervisor combines process, tmux, event age, Git, progress, and explicit result evidence.
Unknown is never automatically treated as dead or safe to replace.
Restart reconciliation preserves decisions, notifications, attempts, and uncertain external effects.
Fault injection proves interrupted effects do not duplicate launches, issues, decisions, or steering.
Recovery procedures are documented for operators.

Resolve issue #55 (MB-009-F006 residual): the latest-attempt authority for a preserved branch is persisted durably, survives controller restart after a later attempt disappears, and rejects recirculated older retirement evidence, with real and fake regression tests.

The operator CLI provides a read-only reconcile report comparing the event store, GitHub issues, worktrees, tmux endpoints, and progress records: it lists mismatches and dependency-ready work, reports unknown (never success) when a source is unreachable, and provably performs no writes.

tasks.title: Complete the reference workflow, operational documentation, and acceptance proof
acceptance_criteria: A scripted workflow covers intake, planning, architecture, issue creation, coding, QA, and completion without live model or network calls.
Restart tests preserve unread notifications, open decisions, uncertain effects, and active work.
Operator views explain active role, tmux endpoint, worktree, SHAs, progress, QA, and blockers.
Protected live evaluations cover Architect ambiguity, Coder recovery, Tester independence, and Coordinator decision fidelity.
Every acceptance criterion in PRD.md is linked to repeatable evidence or an explicitly protected live evaluation.
The operator CLI provides a usage report by role, task, model, and attempt, including launch context size and compaction counts, derived only from recorded telemetry (PRD 12.7).
The reference workflow demonstrates bounded rework escalating to a user decision, and a user-accepted known limitation that stays open as a deferred defect with a linked follow-up issue.

tasks.title: Add a quiet command runner for smoke, preflight, and validators

known_limitations: Shell keywords and shell-only builtins can pass command discovery and behave inconsistently between quiet and verbose modes.
Control characters in the configured log-directory path can break the one-physical-line summary invariant.

acceptance_criteria: scripts/run-quiet.sh <command...> runs the command, writes full stdout and stderr to a log file under ${MILBURN_LOG_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/milburn-logs}, and prints one line with the command, result, duration, and log path.
On a nonzero exit it prints the same line plus the last 40 log lines and exits with the command's exit code; on success it exits 0.
--verbose or MILBURN_VERBOSE=1 streams the command output unchanged.
An unwritable log directory, a missing command, and a nonexistent executable fail closed with a clear message and a nonzero exit; output is never silently discarded.
scripts/run-tests.sh and scripts/smoke-test.sh keep their current behavior and their tests keep passing.
Negative tests for every refusal and failure path are written before the happy path, and every check is exercised with an input that would pass a weaker check but must be rejected.
Behavior is tested through the public command-line interface; nothing in AGENTS.md, bootstrap/README.md, bootstrap/ROOT_PROMPT.md, bootstrap/tasks.json, or the coordinator progress file is modified.

AMEND-004, once effective, accepts the recorded shell keyword/builtin and control-character display limitations for preserved candidate 915e9e98e666339b6075eb0d016c1ea6ab31c339 and waives only the fresh Specification and Standards escalation.

tasks.title: Add a token usage report over Codex rollout logs
acceptance_criteria: scripts/token-report.py <file-or-directory...> reads Codex rollout JSONL files and reports input, cached input, output, and reasoning tokens per session, grouped by role, task, and model, with call counts, compaction counts, and spawn mode (fork_turns) where recorded.
Totals sum per-call usage records, not cumulative thread totals, so repeated cumulative fields are never double counted; the same session file supplied twice is counted once.
Role and task come from the subagent agent_path in session metadata; sessions without it are reported as root.
Output is a deterministic text table, and --json emits machine-readable output; the script only reads logs and never writes inside the repository.
Malformed lines, unknown record types, a truncated final line, and missing usage fields are counted and reported without crashing; they are never silently dropped.
Fixtures are small synthetic rollouts with no real transcripts, credentials, or personal data.
Negative tests for every refusal and failure path are written before the happy path, and every check is exercised with an input that would pass a weaker check but must be rejected.
Behavior is tested through the public command-line interface; nothing in AGENTS.md, bootstrap/README.md, bootstrap/ROOT_PROMPT.md, bootstrap/tasks.json, or the coordinator progress file is modified.

tasks.title: Add the bootstrap configuration file and loader
acceptance_criteria: bootstrap/config.json defines the model ID per role (root and builder gpt-5.6-sol, reviewer gpt-6-sol), reasoning effort (medium), rotation thresholds (context-window percentage 35, absolute token ceiling 100000, maximum rotations), and explicit launcher sandbox and approval fields whose values are null until the user sets them.
scripts/milburn_config.py validate exits nonzero for unknown keys, a missing role, an empty model ID, a non-positive threshold, or a percentage outside 1-100.
scripts/milburn_config.py get <dotted.key> prints one value, and fails with a clear message for an unknown key.
validate --for-launcher fails closed while either launcher permission field is null; the task does not choose those values.
The model IDs live only in this file, and the loader never falls back to another role's model.
Negative tests for every refusal and failure path are written before the happy path, and every check is exercised with an input that would pass a weaker check but must be rejected.
Behavior is tested through the public command-line interface; nothing in AGENTS.md, bootstrap/README.md, bootstrap/ROOT_PROMPT.md, bootstrap/tasks.json, or the coordinator progress file is modified.

tasks.title: Generate worker and reviewer briefs and the root state digest
acceptance_criteria: make-brief.py worker <task> <attempt> writes bootstrap/briefs/<task>-<attempt>.md with the task ID and title, attempt, worktree, branch, base SHA, owned and prohibited paths, Git identity, acceptance criteria, required tests, extracted excerpts of only the PRD and ARCH sections named in an optional spec_refs list on the task record, a short worker-rules block, the six boundary questions, and on resume a summary of the progress file.
When a task has no spec_refs the brief says so explicitly; a spec_refs entry that matches no heading fails closed instead of producing an empty excerpt.
make-brief.py reviewer <task> <attempt> <round> adds the base and candidate or integrated SHAs and the recorded review mode, and for a re-review the prior findings and the fix commit range.

make-brief.py state writes bootstrap/progress/state.md in at most 80 lines: current wave, preflight result, task status table, active workers with branch, worktree, and SHAs, dependency-ready tasks, blockers, and the resume action.
Every generated file embeds a digest of its sources, and make-brief.py check exits nonzero when any brief or state.md is stale; a brief over 16000 characters fails with a clear message.
make-brief.py migrate-history shows what would move from coordinator.md to bootstrap/progress/history/ and writes nothing without --apply; the coordinator, not the worker, runs --apply.
An unknown task or attempt fails closed.
Negative tests for every refusal and failure path are written before the happy path, and every check is exercised with an input that would pass a weaker check but must be rejected.
Behavior is tested through the public command-line interface; nothing in AGENTS.md, bootstrap/README.md, bootstrap/ROOT_PROMPT.md, bootstrap/tasks.json, or the coordinator progress file is modified.

tasks.title: Add the read-only reconcile command
acceptance_criteria: scripts/reconcile.sh compares tasks.json with GitHub issue assignment and lifecycle labels, worktrees and branches, progress files, pending candidates, coordinator pull requests, local and remote Git state, and the amendment preflight, and prints pass or a list of mismatches plus the dependency-ready tasks; full detail goes to a log file.
The command is read-only: tests with a stubbed gh prove that it never edits files, labels, issues, branches, or pull requests and calls only read operations.
When GitHub is unreachable or rate limited the result is unknown and exits nonzero; it never reports a pass it could not check.

Mismatch cases covered: missing issue, label disagreeing with status, closed issue not done, branch without a worktree, worktree without a task, stale candidate SHA, dirty planning file, and local main ahead of or diverged from origin/main.
Tests use a stubbed gh and local repositories only; no network.
Negative tests for every refusal and failure path are written before the happy path, and every check is exercised with an input that would pass a weaker check but must be rejected.
Behavior is tested through the public command-line interface; nothing in AGENTS.md, bootstrap/README.md, bootstrap/ROOT_PROMPT.md, bootstrap/tasks.json, or the coordinator progress file is modified.

tasks.title: Add the scripted candidate integration command
acceptance_criteria: prepare <task> <attempt> <sha> runs the preflight, candidate and trailer verification, the owned-path check (violations are reported, never auto-approved), the task tests and smoke test, a non-squash merge into the ticket's integration branch, and one registry and progress commit under the configured coordinator identity; it refuses to run on a dirty primary checkout.

record-review stores the review mode, risk reason, verdict, and each finding (ID, boundary-question number, file and symbol, severity, round) and returns continue or escalate: escalate when a finding recurs, when a round has no fewer blocking findings than the last round that had findings, when a round adds a new blocking finding in code the last fix touched, or after three fix rounds.

land <task> <attempt> requires a recorded review verdict, passing feedback validation, an unchanged integration SHA, and passing tests; it pushes only the integration branch, builds the pull request body from the records, merges with a merge commit only, verifies origin/main contains the merge commit, fast-forwards the primary checkout, writes the final records in one commit, and applies labels.
status reports the current phase; every subcommand is idempotent and resumes correctly after an interruption, including after the push and before the merge.
The script never pushes to main, never overrides the configured Git identity, never commits when the preflight fails (it restores the files it touched), and refuses ambiguous states.
All tests run against throwaway local repositories, a local bare remote, and a stubbed gh; no network and no real GitHub.

Refusal cases covered first: squash or rebase merge attempted, push to main attempted, changed candidate SHA, missing review verdict, failing feedback validation, dirty checkout, and each escalation rule.
Negative tests for every refusal and failure path are written before the happy path, and every check is exercised with an input that would pass a weaker check but must be rejected.
Behavior is tested through the public command-line interface; nothing in AGENTS.md, bootstrap/README.md, bootstrap/ROOT_PROMPT.md, bootstrap/tasks.json, or the coordinator progress file is modified.

tasks.title: Add the fresh-session root launcher
acceptance_criteria: scripts/run-root.sh starts each root session as a fresh codex exec run with the prompt block from bootstrap/ROOT_PROMPT.md; it never uses codex exec resume for rotation and never passes --ephemeral.

After each run it reads state.md and the reconcile result: it relaunches fresh when rotation was requested, and stops on a recorded blocker, an escalation, no remaining authorized work, or the configured maximum number of rotations.
Sandbox and approval arguments come only from bootstrap/config.json; the launcher refuses to start while either is null.
After an abnormal termination it uses codex exec resume only for crash recovery and marks interrupted workers to restart as new generations from their briefs.
It checks that subagent tools are available in the first run and stops with a clear message if they are not.
Tests use a stub codex executable; the real Codex is never invoked.
Negative tests for every refusal and failure path are written before the happy path, and every check is exercised with an input that would pass a weaker check but must be rejected.
Behavior is tested through the public command-line interface; nothing in AGENTS.md, bootstrap/README.md, bootstrap/ROOT_PROMPT.md, bootstrap/tasks.json, or the coordinator progress file is modified.
